q.t: All mountains, rivers and living things exist on the thin outer layer called the…
q.e: As thin as an apple's skin compared to the apple.

q.t: Which is the hottest planet?
q.e: About 450 °C, due to its thick CO₂ atmosphere.

q.t: Trapping of heat by gases like carbon dioxide is the…
q.e: It keeps Earth warm enough for life.

q.t: The range of distances where water stays liquid is the…
q.e: Not too hot, not too cold.

q.t: The ozone layer blocks…
q.e: Ozone is a three-atom oxygen molecule.

q.t: All the water on Earth is the…
q.e: About 70% of Earth's surface.

q.t: All living beings and where they live make up the…
q.e: Land, water and air.

q.t: A single parent producing exact copies is…
q.e: Bacteria, amoeba, hydra budding.

q.t: Reproductive cells carrying half the genetic material are…
q.e: Sperm and eggs in animals.

q.t: Climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution together are the…
q.e: The three biggest environmental challenges.

q.t: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury, though farther from the Sun?
o: Its thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat
q.e: A strong greenhouse effect.

q.t: Without the greenhouse effect, Earth would be…
q.e: It isn't bad in itself — too much is the danger.

q.t: Why is Earth's size important?
o: Its gravity can hold an atmosphere
q.e: Smaller planets lose their gases.

q.t: Mars's atmosphere compared to Earth's is…
q.e: Mercury has none at all.

q.t: Earth's magnetic field protects us from…
q.e: It pushes many high-energy particles away.

q.t: Why does a nearly circular orbit help life?
o: Sunlight and heat stay nearly steady all year
q.e: No extreme seasonal swings.

q.t: Bamboo and sugarcane spread by…
q.e: That's why you rarely see their seeds.

q.t: Hydra reproduces by…
q.e: Tiny buds break off and become new individuals.

q.t: The Montreal Protocol (1987) reduced…
o: CFCs, helping the ozone layer recover
q.e: A genuine success story.

q.t: The Paris Agreement aims to limit warming to below…
q.e: As of 2025 the world isn't on track.

q.t: Why don't children have double the genetic material of each parent?
q.e: Two halves make one complete set.

q.t: Why do brothers and sisters look different?
o: Each gamete carries a different mix of instructions
q.e: The instructions mix differently every time.

q.t: Reproduction does two jobs:
o: Keeps each kind continuing and lets life adapt
q.e: Small changes over generations can produce new features.

q.t: Camels developing humps to store fat is an example of…
q.e: Small changes that helped them survive deserts.

q.t: Atmospheric greenhouse vs plant greenhouse:
o: Gases absorb Earth's radiation; glass traps warm air
q.e: Both keep warm, by different mechanisms.

q.t: Why does burning fossil fuels add CO₂ Earth can't cope with?
o: It releases carbon locked underground for millions of years
q.e: Plants and plankton can't absorb all the extra.

q.t: If grasses vanished from a grassland, tigers would…
q.e: Biodiversity loss travels up the chain.

q.t: Geodiversity is…
o: Variety of landforms, rocks and soils
q.e: It creates unique habitats.

q.t: Fish and frogs fertilise eggs…
q.e: Sperm and eggs released into water.

q.t: India's Mangalyaan (2013) studied…
o: Mars's atmosphere, surface and past water
q.e: Whether Mars was ever suitable for life.

q.t: Why don't dogs lay eggs or hens give live birth?
o: Each body is built around one strategy for feeding the embryo
q.e: Eggs pack food in advance; live birth supplies it continuously.

q.t: In birds, the embryo is fed by…
q.e: It must last until hatching.

q.t: In most mammals, the embryo develops…
o: Inside the mother's body, fed by her
q.e: The mother supplies food and oxygen until birth.

q.t: Mars lies at the edge of the habitable zone. What has been found?
o: No proof of life, but signs it may once have had water
q.e: Science stays open to new evidence.

q.t: Planaria are studied to understand…
q.e: They regrow from body fragments.

q.t: Cutting a forest can change…
o: Rainfall, soil, air quality and animals
q.e: Everything works together in balance.

q.t: Which statement about the greenhouse effect is correct?
o: Too much of it causes dangerous warming
q.e: The right amount keeps Earth habitable.

q.t: Soil nutrients like nitrogen and potassium come from…
o: Breakdown of rocks and remains of living things
q.e: The crust provides almost everything life needs.

q.t: Which action helps protect the climate?
q.e: Also energy efficiency and greener travel.

q.t: Soil pollution from excess fertilisers can…
o: Reduce crop yield and spread harm through food chains
q.e: Poor waste disposal does the same.
